clue.text: Respect and endless pride so involved in this

definitions.text: Respect and endless pride so involved in this

indicators.note: involved means tangled up together, so these letters are mixed into a new order
endless says the word pride loses its final letter

parts.note: taken as written before its last letter goes

explanation.surface: Respect and pride, mixed together, are what a team spirit is made of.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' trims PRIDE to PRID; 'involved' shuffles RESPECT + PRID + SO into the answer, and the whole clue also describes it: respect and pride bound up together.
explanation.definitionFit: Team spirit, the shared pride and loyalty of a group, is what the clue describes as respect and pride bound together.

clue.text: Busy in Oxford, disorganized reader moves on around university

indicators.note: around says the shuffled letters sit on either side of the university letter
disorganized means put out of order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A muddled reader drifting on and around an Oxford college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Busy' is old police slang for a detective; Inspector Morse, of the TV series, works in Oxford. 'disorganized' shuffles READER MOVES ON, and 'around' puts that shuffle round U.
explanation.definitionFit: Inspector Morse, whose first name is Endeavour, is the fictional detective (a busy) of Oxford.

clue.text: In confusion, unknown left small screen part

indicators.note: In says the unknown letter goes inside the word for confusion

parts.note: pie, or pi, is a printer's term for type jumbled into confusion
X is the classic mathematical unknown

explanation.surface: A muddle in which some unknown thing left a tiny bit of a TV screen.
explanation.walkthrough: PIE, a printer's word for spilled and jumbled type, takes X inside, then L follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A pixel is one of the tiny dots making up a television or computer display, the small screen.

clue.text: Craft useful to party organizers

definitions.meaning: a ship built to break a channel through ice is this kind of vessel
a game or remark that gets strangers talking at a party

explanation.surface: A boat that party planners would find handy.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a ship that clears frozen seas and an activity that relaxes guests meeting for the first time.

clue.text: Does victim of this crime forgive the errant perpetrator?

definitions.text: Does victim of this crime forgive the errant perpetrator?

parts.words: Does victim of this crime forgive the errant perpetrator?
parts.note: plays on 'to err is human, to forgive divine': the victim of this crime is God, who as the divine one would forgive whoever erred

explanation.surface: A question about whether the victim of some crime pardons the wrongdoer.
explanation.walkthrough: Pope's line 'To err is human, to forgive divine' is the key: the victim here is divine.
explanation.definitionFit: The killing of a god is the crime whose victim is the divine being who forgives.

clue.text: Secret agent finally put in picture following announcement

indicators.note: following says the picture part comes after the announcement

parts.note: a cry is a call or public announcement, as by a town crier

indicators.note: put in says the letter goes inside the short word for picture

parts.note: pic is an informal short form of picture

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the word agent

explanation.surface: A spy's last move is to get into a picture after a public statement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Secret agent' reads as one phrase, but 'Secret' alone is the definition. 'finally' gives agent's last letter, 'put in' places it in the picture word, and 'following' sets that after the announcement.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic means hidden or mysterious, which is what a secret thing is.

clue.text: Growth of bank career

definitions.meaning: a reedy marsh plant growing on a river bank
to career is to hurtle or dash headlong

explanation.surface: How a bank's business expands as a profession.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bank' suggests money and 'career' a job; really the bank is a riverside and career is a verb of speed.
explanation.definitionFit: The same word is a waterside plant and a verb for hurrying at speed, just as careering does.

clue.text: Recorded conflict over, as result of successful shooting from both sides

definitions.text: result of successful shooting from both sides

parts.note: scored means recorded, as points are noted on a scorecard

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the word for conflict is read backwards

parts.note: war is armed conflict

explanation.surface: A war is logged as finished, as both sides shoot successfully.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns WAR into RAW. In football a score draw is a drawn game where both teams scored, important on the British football pools.
explanation.definitionFit: A drawn match in which both teams scored goals is what both sides shooting successfully produces.

clue.text: Religious campaign in shoe works

parts.note: an oxford is a laced leather shoe
the movement is the works, the inner mechanism, of a watch or clock

explanation.surface: A church crusade carried on in a shoe factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'works' looks like a factory or a verb; it is a watch's mechanism.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oxford Movement was a nineteenth-century High Church revival within the Church of England.

clue.text: Nothing sinister about this skill?

parts.note: sinister is Latin for left-handed, and its opposite, Latin dexter, means right-handed; the skill named here comes from the right hand

explanation.surface: An assurance that some talent is wholly innocent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sinister' looks like 'evil' but works in its Latin sense, left; the skill takes its name from the Latin for right.
explanation.definitionFit: Dexterity is manual skill, its name rooted in the Latin for right-handed, the opposite of sinister.

clue.text: Brave types proceed legally in hearing

indicators.note: in hearing says the word is judged by how it sounds when spoken

parts.note: to sue is to take legal proceedings against someone

explanation.surface: Courageous people going to court at a court hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brave' is a noun here: a Native American warrior. 'hearing' looks like a court hearing but signals the sound-alike.
explanation.definitionFit: A brave is a Native American warrior, and the Sioux are a Native American people of the plains.

clue.text: Daughter in real trouble needed psychiatrist

indicators.note: in says the daughter letter sits inside the rearranged letters
trouble means disturbed, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A daughter in real distress needed a shrink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' shuffles REAL into ALER, and 'in' places D inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred Adler was an Austrian psychiatrist, founder of individual psychology.

clue.text: Enthusiastic about nothing on modest unsuitable contract

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as printed and scanned, 'Enthusiastic about nothing on modest unsuitable contract (4)', gives the definition 'Enthusiastic about' but no wordplay found that builds the letters; exact-text search gave nothing.
annotationWithheld.clue: Enthusiastic about nothing on modest unsuitable contract

clue.text: Conclusions reached by board move team to protest

indicators.note: conclusions are endings, so the last letter of each of the following words is taken

explanation.surface: The board reaches its conclusions and moves the team to protest.
explanation.definitionFit: A demo is a public demonstration, a march or rally held to protest.

clue.text: Call to start fighting slightly mistimed

definitions.meaning: the referee's cry in boxing that sends the helpers out of the ring as a round begins
out by a few seconds, a tiny error of timing

explanation.surface: A signal for fighting to begin, given a little late.
explanation.definitionFit: The boxing call clearing a fighter's helpers also reads as being a few seconds off, slightly late or early.

clue.text: Travelling in vehicle seen from house

definitions.meaning: visible to the theatre audience, the house, while performing

explanation.surface: Riding in a car that can be seen from home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'house' is a theatre's audience; 'vehicle' is a stagecoach.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both aboard a stagecoach and performing in view of a theatre audience.

clue.text: Hard cash as part of royalty

definitions.meaning: a British gold coin, once worth one pound
a monarch, a king or queen

explanation.surface: Coins forming part of a royalty payment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'royalty' looks like an author's payment, matching 'cash'; it means kings and queens.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a gold pound coin and also a reigning monarch, one member of royalty.

clue.text: Got over being released

definitions.meaning: jumped over without touching, as a horse does a fence
freed, as of a charge, or let go

explanation.surface: Someone recovered once let out.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both jumped clean over an obstacle and freed or acquitted.

clue.text: Needing resort. I arrive in seaside area

indicators.note: resort read as re-sort, so the letters need sorting into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone arriving who needs a holiday resort by the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' looks like a holiday place, matching the Riviera; split as re-sort it orders a reshuffle of I ARRIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Riviera is the Mediterranean coastline of France and Italy, famous for its beach towns.

clue.text: Old style firm supporting new trade

indicators.note: supporting in a down clue means the firm goes underneath, after the new trade
new means remade, so these letters are formed afresh in another order

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: An established company backing a fresh line of business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' makes ARTDE from TRADE; 'supporting' puts CO beneath it.
explanation.definitionFit: Art deco is a decorative design movement of the 1920s and 1930s, a period style now old.

clue.text: Reference book identifying international medical group's doctor

parts.note: the WHO, the World Health Organization, with the possessive
Doctor Who, the time-travelling TV doctor

explanation.surface: A directory naming a global health body's physician.
explanation.walkthrough: The WHO is the World Health Organization; the Doctor is the hero of the British TV series Doctor Who.
explanation.definitionFit: Who's Who is an annual reference book of short biographies of notable people.

clue.text: One child inhabiting Washington or Kansas City

indicators.note: inhabiting says the child pieces live inside the state abbreviation

parts.note: WA is the postal abbreviation for Washington state
I is the Roman numeral for one
a chit is a young child, often a pert girl

explanation.surface: A child living in either Washington or Kansas City.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kansas City' looks like the Missouri city; it means a city in Kansas.
explanation.definitionFit: Wichita is the largest city in the US state of Kansas.

clue.text: Consent to artist showing ladies' fingers

parts.note: OK means agreement or consent
RA, Royal Academician, is the stock crossword artist

explanation.surface: Agreeing to a painter displaying some women's hands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ladies' fingers' is a British name for the vegetable, not a body part.
explanation.definitionFit: Okra pods are known in Britain as ladies' fingers, from their long slender shape.

clue.text: Contents of ad about hearing aids

indicators.note: contents means the inside, so the word for ad loses its first and last letters

parts.note: a notice is an advertisement or announcement

explanation.surface: What's in an advert for hearing aids.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hearing aids' reads as one product; split it, with 'about hearing' the definition and 'aids' a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Otic is a medical adjective meaning relating to the ear.

clue.text: Led up to reform, like Henry IV?

indicators.note: reform means form again, so these letters are put in a different order

explanation.surface: A king prompted to bring in changes.
explanation.walkthrough: Shakespeare's Henry IV is a play in two parts, so it is twofold.
explanation.definitionFit: Duple means double or in two parts, as Shakespeare's two-part Henry IV is.

clue.text: Foreign soldier fuelling uprising?

annotationWithheld.why: Clue 'Foreign soldier fuelling uprising? (5)': P(OIL)U needs 'fuelling' as both OIL and the insertion indicator, a word doing two jobs.

clue.text: Talent needed to make a presentation

definitions.meaning: a present is what is handed over at a presentation ceremony

explanation.surface: Ability that a speaker needs to give a talk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'presentation' looks like a talk; it is a ceremony of handing over a present.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a natural knack and a present handed over.

clue.text: Why rhymes are needed for this literary genre

definitions.text: Why rhymes are needed for this literary genre

parts.words: Why rhymes are needed for this literary genre
parts.note: each syllable of the genre's short name sounds like a word rhyming with why, so it is made of two such rhymes

explanation.surface: Why some kind of writing must use rhymes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Why' looks like a question; it is the word both halves of the genre's name rhyme with.
explanation.definitionFit: Science fiction, abbreviated, is a literary genre of futuristic stories.

clue.text: Reduce English dish male is tucking into

indicators.note: tucking into says the male and is go inside the word for dish

parts.note: a pie is a baked dish
a tom is a male cat

explanation.surface: Cut back on an English pie a man is eating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucking into' suggests eating but signals insertion: TOM IS goes into PIE.
explanation.definitionFit: To epitomise is to sum up in brief, reducing something to its essentials.

clue.text: Confidence of all the people preserving organization

definitions.meaning: faith held by the whole nation
a body that conserves historic houses and countryside

explanation.surface: Faith of the whole populace in a body that protects things.
explanation.walkthrough: The National Trust is a British charity that owns and preserves historic houses, gardens and land.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase reads as a nation's faith and names the British heritage conservation charity.
